question: Under paragraph 4.2.2(ii) of the Master Circular, what minimum Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio must a bank maintain on an ongoing basis?
options: 2.5% of risk-weighted assets
7.0% of risk-weighted assets
9.0% of risk-weighted assets
5.5% of risk-weighted assets
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.2.2(ii)
source_excerpt: Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital must be at least 5.5% of risk-weighted assets (RWAs) i.e., for credit risk + market risk + operational risk on an ongoing basis.

question: What does paragraph 4.2.2(iii) set as the minimum Tier 1 capital ratio, and what maximum Additional Tier 1 capital does it allow within that ratio?
options: 6.5% of RWAs with Additional Tier 1 capped at 2.0%
8.0% of RWAs with Additional Tier 1 capped at 1.5%
9.0% of RWAs with Additional Tier 1 capped at 2.0%
7% of RWAs with Additional Tier 1 capped at 1.5%
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.2.2(iii)
source_excerpt: Tier 1 capital must be at least 7% of RWAs on an ongoing basis. Thus, within the minimum Tier 1 capital, Additional Tier 1 capital can be admitted maximum at 1.5% of RWAs.

question: According to paragraph 4.2.2(iv), what minimum total capital must a bank hold, and how much Tier 2 capital may be admitted within it?
options: 11.5% of RWAs with Tier 2 admitted up to 2.5%
8.0% of RWAs with Tier 2 admitted up to 1.5%
9% of RWAs with Tier 2 admitted up to 2%
10% of RWAs with Tier 2 admitted up to 1.5%
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.2.2(iv)
source_excerpt: Total Capital (Tier 1 Capital plus Tier 2 Capital) must be at least 9% of RWAs on an ongoing basis. Thus, within the minimum CRAR of 9%, Tier 2 capital can be admitted maximum up to 2%.

question: What does paragraph 15.2.1 require every bank to maintain above the regulatory minimum capital requirement, and of what form is it?
options: A capital conservation buffer of 2.5%, comprised of Common Equity Tier 1 capital
A capital conservation buffer of 2.5%, comprised of Additional Tier 1 capital
A countercyclical capital buffer of 1.5%, comprised of Tier 2 capital
A capital conservation buffer of 4.0%, comprised of Common Equity Tier 1 capital
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 15.2.1
source_excerpt: Banks are required to maintain a capital conservation buffer of 2.5%, comprised of Common Equity Tier 1 capital, above the regulatory minimum capital requirement

question: How does paragraph 4.1 state the minimum Pillar 1 Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio, and how does it treat the capital buffers?
options: 9% on an on-going basis, other than capital conservation buffer and countercyclical capital buffer
9% on an on-going basis including both the capital conservation and countercyclical buffers
11.5% on an on-going basis including the capital conservation buffer
8% on an on-going basis excluding every capital buffer
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.1
source_excerpt: Banks shall maintain a minimum Pillar 1 Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) of 9% on an on-going basis (other than capital conservation buffer and countercyclical capital buffer etc.).

question: How does the footnote to paragraph 4.2.1 distinguish going-concern capital from gone-concern capital?
options: Going-concern capital absorbs losses only in a situation of liquidation, while gone-concern capital absorbs losses without triggering bankruptcy
Both going-concern and gone-concern capital absorb losses only when the bank is liquidated
Going-concern capital absorbs losses without triggering bankruptcy; gone-concern capital absorbs losses only in liquidation
Gone-concern capital is the capital that absorbs losses in the normal course of business
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.2.1, footnote 5
source_excerpt: From regulatory capital perspective, going-concern capital is the capital which can absorb losses without triggering bankruptcy of the bank. Gone-concern capital is the capital which will absorb losses only in a situation of liquidation of the bank.

question: Under paragraph 4.4.1, from which component of capital must goodwill and all other intangible assets be deducted?
options: From Tier 2 capital only, to the extent it exceeds 2% of RWAs
From Additional Tier 1 capital, at the discretion of the bank
From Tier 1 capital, but only the amount above 10% of capital funds
From Common Equity Tier 1 capital
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.4.1(i)
source_excerpt: Goodwill and all other intangible assets should be deducted from Common Equity Tier 1 capital including any goodwill included in the valuation of significant investments in the capital of banking, financial and insurance entities which are outside the scope of regulatory consolidation.

question: What minimum leverage ratio does paragraph 16.2.2 prescribe for domestic systemically important banks and for other banks respectively?
options: 5% for D-SIBs and 4% for other banks
3% for D-SIBs and 2.5% for other banks
4% for every bank irrespective of systemic importance
4% for D-SIBs and 3.5% for other banks
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 16.2.2
source_excerpt: The minimum Leverage Ratio shall be 4% for Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) and 3.5% for other banks

question: How does paragraph 16.2.1 define the Basel III leverage ratio?
options: Common Equity Tier 1 capital divided by total risk-weighted assets, expressed as a percentage
Tier 2 capital divided by the exposure measure, expressed as a decimal fraction
The capital measure divided by the exposure measure, expressed as a percentage
Tier 1 capital divided by the capital conservation buffer, expressed as a percentage
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 16.2.1
source_excerpt: The Basel III leverage ratio is defined as the capital measure (the numerator) divided by the exposure measure (the denominator), with this ratio expressed as a percentage.

question: Which capital measure does paragraph 16.3 specify as the numerator to be used for the leverage ratio?
options: Common Equity Tier 1 capital of the risk-based capital framework
Total capital comprising Tier 1 and Tier 2 of the risk-based framework
Additional Tier 1 capital of the risk-based capital framework
Tier 1 capital of the risk-based capital framework
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 16.3
source_excerpt: The capital measure for the leverage ratio is the Tier 1 capital of the risk-based capital framework

question: According to paragraph 16.4.1, which four groups of exposures together make up a bank's total leverage ratio exposure measure?
options: On-balance sheet exposures and derivative exposures only, with securities financing transactions excluded
On-balance sheet exposures, derivative exposures, SFT exposures and off-balance sheet items
Credit risk, market risk, operational risk and counterparty credit risk exposures
Only the on-balance sheet non-derivative exposures recorded at accounting value
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 16.4.1(iii)
source_excerpt: A bank's total exposure measure is the sum of the following exposures: (a) on-balance sheet exposures; (b) derivative exposures; (c) securities financing transaction (SFT) exposures; and (d) off-balance sheet (OBS) items.

question: Under paragraph 3.1(a), which entities are excluded when capital adequacy is measured at the consolidated (Group) level?
options: Those engaged in insurance and any non-financial activities
Subsidiaries engaged in banking and financial services
Joint ventures and associates incorporated outside India
Wholly owned subsidiaries of foreign banks operating in India
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 3.1(a)
source_excerpt: capital adequacy ratio requirements, which measure the capital adequacy of a bank based on its capital strength and risk profile after consolidating the assets and liabilities of its subsidiaries / joint ventures / associates etc. except those engaged in insurance and any non-financial activities

question: What does paragraph 3.4.1 direct about the consolidation of subsidiaries for the purpose of capital adequacy?
options: Only insurance subsidiaries should be consolidated for capital adequacy
No subsidiary should be consolidated; only solo level capital adequacy applies
All banking and other financial subsidiaries except insurance and non-financial ones should be fully consolidated
Every subsidiary of the bank, including those engaged in insurance and non-financial activities, should be fully consolidated
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 3.4.1
source_excerpt: All banking and other financial subsidiaries except subsidiaries engaged in insurance and any non-financial activities (both regulated and unregulated) should be fully consolidated for the purpose of capital adequacy

question: How does paragraph 3.4.2 treat the equity and other regulatory capital investments in insurance and non-financial subsidiaries?
options: They are added to the Common Equity Tier 1 capital of the consolidated banking group
They are risk-weighted at 100% in the consolidated capital adequacy framework
They are deducted from consolidated regulatory capital of the group
They are recognised as Additional Tier 1 capital of the parent bank
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 3.4.2
source_excerpt: The equity and other regulatory capital investments in the insurance and non-financial subsidiaries will be deducted from consolidated regulatory capital of the group.

question: According to paragraph 3.5.1, what must be done at solo level with investments in the capital instruments of subsidiaries that are consolidated in the group's financial statements?
options: They shall be deducted from the corresponding capital instruments issued by the bank
They shall be added to the Common Equity Tier 1 capital of the bank
They shall be deducted only from the capital conservation buffer
They need not be deducted at solo level because the group already consolidates those subsidiaries
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 3.5.1
source_excerpt: In addition, investments in the capital instruments of the subsidiaries, which are consolidated in the consolidated financial statements of the group, shall be deducted from the corresponding capital instruments issued by the bank.

question: What minimum capital adequacy ratio does paragraph 3.3 require a foreign bank's Wholly Owned Subsidiary to maintain for an initial period after it commences operations?
options: 8 per cent on a continuous basis for an initial period of five years from the date of commencement of its operations
10 per cent on a continuous basis for an initial period of three years from the commencement of its operations
12 per cent on an ongoing basis for the first year and 10 per cent thereafter
9 per cent for an initial period of two years from the commencement of its operations
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 3.3
source_excerpt: WOS shall, however, maintain a minimum capital adequacy ratio, on a continuous basis for an initial period of three years from the commencement of its operations, at 10 per cent.

question: Under paragraph 4.2.3.1, at what discount may revaluation reserves arising on revaluation of a bank's property be reckoned as Common Equity Tier 1 capital?
options: At a discount of 45 per cent, subject to conditions
At a discount of 25 per cent, subject to conditions
At a discount of 10 per cent, subject to conditions
At a discount of 55 per cent, subject to conditions
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.2.3.1.A(vi)
source_excerpt: Revaluation reserves arising out of change in the carrying amount of a bank's property consequent upon its revaluation may be reckoned as CET1 capital at a discount of 55 per cent, subject to meeting the following conditions

question: Which of the following is listed in paragraph 4.2.4.1 as an element of Additional Tier 1 capital for Indian banks?
options: Debt capital instruments complying with the requirements of Annex 5
Preference share capital instruments complying with the requirements of Annex 6
General provisions and loss reserves held against future unidentified losses
Perpetual Non-Cumulative Preference Shares (PNCPS) complying with Annex 3
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.2.4.1.A(i)
source_excerpt: Perpetual Non-Cumulative Preference Shares (PNCPS), which comply with the regulatory requirements as specified in Annex 3

question: Under paragraph 4.2.5.1, up to what maximum amount are general provisions and loss reserves admitted as Tier 2 capital under the standardized approach?
options: 0.6% of credit risk weighted assets, the limit that applies under the Internal Ratings Based approach
2.0% of total risk weighted assets under the standardized approach
1.25% of the total credit risk weighted assets under the standardized approach
1.5% of credit risk weighted assets under the standardized approach
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.2.5.1.A(i)
source_excerpt: However, these items together will be admitted as Tier 2 capital up to a maximum of 1.25% of the total credit risk weighted assets under the standardized approach

question: What does paragraph 4.2.5.1 provide about the Investment Fluctuation Reserve and its inclusion in regulatory capital?
options: It qualifies for Tier 2 capital only up to 1.25% of credit risk weighted assets
It qualifies for inclusion in Tier 2 capital without any ceiling
It must be deducted from Common Equity Tier 1 capital in full
It qualifies only for inclusion in Additional Tier 1 capital
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.2.5.1.A(i)(b)
source_excerpt: Investment Fluctuation Reserve shall also qualify for inclusion in Tier 2 capital, without any ceiling

question: Which of the following is listed in paragraph 4.2.3.1 as an element of Common Equity Tier 1 capital for Indian banks?
options: Head Office borrowings in foreign currency kept in separate Indian books
General provisions held against future, presently unidentified losses
Perpetual Debt Instruments complying with the requirements of Annex 4
Statutory reserves
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.2.3.1.A
source_excerpt: Common shares (paid-up equity capital) issued by the bank which meet the criteria for classification as common shares for regulatory purposes as given in Annex 1; (ii) Stock surplus (share premium) resulting from the issue of common shares; (iii) Statutory reserves;

question: How does paragraph 4.4.2(i) require deferred tax assets associated with accumulated losses and similar assets to be treated?
options: They shall be deducted in full from CET1 capital
They may be recognised in CET1 capital up to 10% of CET1 capital
They shall be deducted from Tier 2 capital of the bank
They shall be risk-weighted at 250% and retained in Tier 1
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.4.2(i)
source_excerpt: Deferred tax assets (DTAs) associated with accumulated losses and other such assets shall be deducted in full, from CET1 capital.

question: What does paragraph 4.4.2(ii) permit for deferred tax assets that relate to timing differences rather than accumulated losses?
options: They must be deducted in full from CET1 capital under all circumstances without any exception
They may be recognised in CET1 capital up to 15% of a bank's CET1 capital at the discretion of banks
They may be recognised in CET1 capital up to 10% of a bank's CET1 capital, at the discretion of banks
They may be recognised in Tier 2 capital up to 10% of Tier 2 capital
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.4.2(ii)
source_excerpt: DTAs which relate to timing differences (other than those related to accumulated losses) may, instead of full deduction from CET1 capital, be recognised in the CET1 capital up to 10% of a bank's CET1 capital, at the discretion of banks

question: How does paragraph 4.4.8(i) treat a bank's investment in its own shares?
options: It is tantamount to repayment of capital and must be knocked off from the bank's capital
It may be included in Additional Tier 1 capital at the discretion of the bank
It counts as Common Equity Tier 1 capital if held for more than five working days
It is deducted from Tier 2 capital only, and only when the bank holds it through mutual funds or index funds
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.4.8(i)
source_excerpt: Investment in a bank's own shares is tantamount to repayment of capital and therefore, it is necessary to knock-off such investment from the bank's capital with a view to improving the bank's quality of capital

question: Under paragraph 4.4.9.2(A), how are reciprocal cross holdings of capital in banking, financial and insurance entities treated?
options: They are recognised in Tier 1 capital up to 10% of the bank's capital funds
They are risk-weighted at 100% when held in the banking book
Such holdings of capital will be fully deducted
They are deducted only from Tier 2 capital of the investee entity
source: Master Circular - Basel III Capital Regulations, RBI/2025-26/08, DOR.CAP.REC.2/21.06.201/2025-26, April 01, 2025, paragraph 4.4.9.2(A)
source_excerpt: Reciprocal cross holdings of capital might result in artificially inflating the capital position of banks. Such holdings of capital will be fully deducted.
